title: A protocol for gene expression analysis of chondrocytes from bovine osteochondral plugs used for biotribological applications
author: Bauer, Niculescu-Morzsa, et al.

steps.title: Prepare osteochondral plugs
steps.instruction: Process bovine knee to obtain osteochondral plugs and store them until further use.

substeps.instruction: Dissect bovine knee with a scalpel to open the joint.
Punch out osteochondral (OC) plugs from the medial condyle, selecting mostly flat areas.
While unscrewing from the punch, mark each OC plug at the bone side to indicate collagen‑fibril orientation for later mechanical or biotribological testing.
Place each OC plug in a well of a 12‑well plate and overlay with PBS containing antibiotics.
Wash the plugs for 2 h in a shaker (Enviro‑Genie; settings 12:24; 37 °C) to remove fat and bone particles.
Incubate the plugs for up to 1 week in growth medium supplemented with antibiotics, antimycotic and vitamin C until they are needed for mechanical, biotribological or stimulation experiments.
If transport is required, conserve the plugs or cartilage in RNAlater™ for up to 1 week at 4 °C before RNA isolation.

steps.title: Harvest and mince cartilage
steps.instruction: After treatment or stimulation, cut the cartilage off the bone and chop it into pieces of approximately 2 mm³.

steps.title: Lyse tissue in MagNA Lyser tube
steps.instruction: Transfer the minced cartilage pieces to a MagNA Lyser tube containing 300 µl lysis buffer (RNeasy Fibrous Tissue Kit) with 1 % β‑mercaptoethanol added.

steps.title: Freeze samples in liquid nitrogen
steps.instruction: Immediately freeze the tubes in liquid nitrogen.

steps.title: Thaw and homogenize tissue
steps.instruction: Thaw the frozen tubes for 2 min, then place them in the MagNA Lyser and run four homogenization cycles.

substeps.instruction: Run the MagNA Lyser at 6500 rpm for 20 s.
Cool the tube for 2 min at 4 °C on the device’s cooling plate.
Repeat the run‑cool sequence three more times (total of four cycles).

steps.title: Add proteinase K mixture and incubate
steps.instruction: To each disrupted sample add 20 µl proteinase K and 580 µl RNase‑free water, then incubate at 55 °C for 30 min.

steps.title: Centrifuge and collect supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tubes for 3 min at 10 000 g and transfer the clear supernatant to a new 1.5 ml tube.

steps.title: Add ethanol to lysate
steps.instruction: Add 0.5 volumes of 90–100 % ethanol to the supernatant and mix gently.

steps.title: Load lysate onto RNeasy column
steps.instruction: Bind RNA to the RNeasy Mini column by loading the lysate in portions.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 700 µl of the ethanol‑mixed lysate to the column and centrifuge 15 s at 8000 g.
Discard the flow‑through and repeat the loading step until the entire lysate has been applied.

steps.title: Wash column with Buffer RW1
steps.instruction: Add 350 µl Buffer RW1 to the column and centrifuge 15 s at 8000 g; discard the flow‑through.

steps.title: DNase treatment of bound RNA
steps.instruction: Prepare a DNase mix by combining 10 µl DNase stock with 70 µl Buffer RDD, add it to the column membrane, and incubate 15 min at room temperature (20–30 °C).

steps.title: Second wash with Buffer RW1
steps.instruction: Add 350 µl Buffer RW1 to the column and centrifuge 15 s at 8000 g; discard the flow‑through.

steps.title: First wash with Buffer RPE
steps.instruction: Add 500 µl Buffer RPE to the column and centrifuge 15 s at 8000 g; discard the flow‑through.

steps.title: Second wash with Buffer RPE
steps.instruction: Add another 500 µl Buffer RPE and centrifuge 2 min at 8000 g; discard the flow‑through.

steps.title: Dry spin column
steps.instruction: Place the column in a new 2 ml collection tube and centrifuge at full speed for 1 min to remove residual buffer.

steps.title: Elute RNA with RNase‑free water
steps.instruction: Transfer the column to a fresh 1.5 ml tube, add 30 µl RNase‑free water directly onto the membrane, and centrifuge 1 min at 8000 g to collect the eluate.

steps.title: Store RNA at –80 °C
steps.instruction: Store the purified RNA at –80 °C until it is needed for cDNA synthesis.
